methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic information units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two sets of information.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Data is shifted in MSB first when shift_ena is 1
The number in the shift register is decremented when count_ena is 1
Behavior when both shift_ena and count_ena are 1 is a don't-care
If the register value is already 0, it wraps around to 15
If both shift_ena and count_ena are 1, the shift operation takes precedence
Module has clk, shift_ena, count_ena, data inputs and q[3:0] output
spec_atomic_units: Implements a 4-bit shift register
Implements a synchronous down counter
Data is shifted in MSB first when shift_ena is 1
The number in the shift register is decremented when count_ena is 1
Behavior when both shift_ena and count_ena are 1 is a don't-care
If the register value is already 0, it wraps around to 15
If both shift_ena and count_ena are 1, the shift operation takes precedence
Module has clk, shift_ena, count_ena, data inputs and q[3:0] output
shift_ena has setup and hold time requirements with respect to clk
count_ena has setup and hold time requirements with respect to clk
data has setup and hold time requirements with respect to clk
q is updated on the rising edge of clk
q is declared as a reg [3:0]
q[3] <= data when shifting
q[2] <= q[3] (previous state) when shifting
q[1] <= q[2] (previous state) when shifting
q[0] <= q[1] (previous state) when shifting
Output 'q' is decremented by 1 when counting
shift register implemented using D flip-flops
A 4-bit subtractor (for the down counter functionality)
A multiplexer to select between the shift register output, the down counter output, and the current state
select[0] = !shift_ena & count_ena
select[1] = shift_ena
next_q[3] = (shift_ena) ? data : ((count_ena & !shift_ena) ? (q[3:0] - 1)[3] : q[3])
next_q[2] = (shift_ena) ? q[3] : ((count_ena & !shift_ena) ? (q[3:0] - 1)[2] : q[2])
next_q[1] = (shift_ena) ? q[2] : ((count_ena & !shift_ena) ? (q[3:0] - 1)[1] : q[1])
next_q[0] = (shift_ena) ? q[1] : ((count_ena & !shift_ena) ? (q[3:0] - 1)[0] : q[0])
